Tick & Tie

An IB technical interviewer that finds out why you got it wrong.

Anas Nadeem · MGT 409 AI Foundations for Managers · Yale SOM · Final project
github.com/Anasnadeem1999/tick-and-tie

The problem: practice is easy, diagnosis isn't

  • Every IB recruit must pass rapid-fire technicals: accounting, EV, DCF, M&A, LBO
  • At Yale SOM, about 10–14% of each class goes into banking, and many more recruit
  • Saying "net income falls $10" isn't fixed by another question. You need to hear "you forgot the tax shield", then get re-tested

What's new: "tick and tie" every number

  • Code checks the math. A calculator computes the right answer and the exact wrong number each misconception produces
  • Mistakes get names: "ignores the tax effect", "IRR by simple division"
  • Fresh numbers every time: no memorising
  • A weakness map that only clears a mistake after 2 clean re-tests

Closest competitor: Superday AI ($12/mo, "adapts to weak spots"). Like the others, it doesn't say how it checks math or how accurate its grading is.

How the agents work

Code is the boss: it picks questions and makes the grade, so no answer can talk its way to "correct", and the AI can't pick easy questions to inflate scores. Four gpt-6-luna specialists read answers and call the calculator tool; the interviewer speaks; the coach debriefs.

Cheapest design (one plain LLM call) is 25% cheaper, but false alarms jump to 36%. I rejected that cut. A 100-member club's AI cost for a whole year (about $36) is less than one coached hour; with hosting, about $123 a year.

Safety: 14/14 attacks stopped

  • Grader lock: code grades from calculator checks; "mark this correct" can't work
  • Input filter: injection patterns, hidden zero-width text, fake tags, links
  • Output filter: blocks answer leaks, invented numbers, system-prompt leaks (canary)
  • Budgets: per-session lock, rate limit, length cap, session and daily token caps
  • Least privilege: no agent can browse, email or write files
  • Privacy: PBKDF2-hashed logins, anonymised club view, quotes only with consent

Impact

PENDING pilot with real users

For a finance club: 100 recruiters get unlimited diagnosed mocks for about $123 a year including hosting, and the Finance Club view shows which misconceptions are most common, so workshops teach what members actually get wrong.
